clue.text: Bob breaks rules and admits defeat

indicators.note: breaks means one piece splits the other open, here a coin cutting into a verb

parts.note: to rule as a monarch is to reign, so rules gives reigns
a bob was the old shilling, abbreviated S (from Latin solidus)

explanation.surface: A rule-breaker named Bob finally owns up and concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is the old British shilling, S, which 'breaks' into REIGNS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign a game, as in chess, is to concede defeat before the end.

clue.text: One's entertained by bands with revolting acts

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rings are circular bands
one is I, and one's is read as I plus 's, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone is hosted by pop groups along with their rebellious stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', I + S, which sits inside RINGS after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisings or rebellions are revolts, so revolting acts in the sense of rebelling.

clue.text: Trousers almost all will wear out east

indicators.note: almost all of a word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: will and shall are both future auxiliaries, so will gives shall

indicators.note: out signals the following item is removed from the word before it

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone will put on trousers out east, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' trims SHALL to SHAL; 'out' removes E (east) from WEAR to leave WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalwar are the loose trousers of South Asian dress, worn with a kameez.

clue.text: Information on centre of development area somewhere in Italy

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Facts about the heart of a building project in an Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information ('the gen'). DEVELOPMENT has eleven letters; its central sixth letter is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a port city in northwest Italy, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Prescott a false witness?

indicators.note: false suggests the letters are not genuine as arranged and must be reworked

explanation.surface: Is the politician Prescott giving unreliable evidence in court?
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was a British Deputy Prime Minister; 'false' rearranges PRESCOTT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, one who witnesses an event.

clue.text: Shown one little boy carrying another

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward, a little boy's name
another little boy, here Vince, short for Vincent

explanation.surface: A small boy is pictured giving another a piggyback.
explanation.walkthrough: Both boys are short names: ED holds VINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display it, so evinced is a synonym of shown.

clue.text: Eastern republic's flipping weird

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: An eastern state is said to be downright strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, as in 'flipping weird', but it is the reversal signal on the republic's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, a close synonym of weird.

clue.text: Editor in a Polish novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor appears in a book written in Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is the long-serving editor of Private Eye, the British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Hislop has edited the magazine Private Eye since 1986, a famous editor.

clue.text: Smart attempt to encircle a city

indicators.note: to encircle is to surround, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart
a go is an attempt, as in have a go

explanation.surface: A stylish bid to surround a metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart attempt' together forms the outer piece, and 'to encircle' wraps it round A at the point where the two words meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the large American city on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Be sidetracked when groom holds serving man up

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to groom a horse or person is to dress them, make them tidy

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American serving soldier

explanation.surface: A groom loses focus while holding a servant aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving man' suggests a waiter but is the American soldier; 'up' turns him round inside the groom's word, giving IG.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject, to be sidetracked.

clue.text: Native American playwright born in France

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright
née is French for born, used for a maiden name

explanation.surface: A Native American dramatist was born in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are an Algonquian-speaking Native American people.

clue.text: One behind Inspector Rebus with good position in hierarchy

parts.note: Ian Rankin is the novelist who created the Edinburgh detective Inspector Rebus

explanation.surface: The creator of a fictional detective has a fine standing in the police hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One behind' means the author behind the character, not someone standing behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is one's place or rank in an ordered list or hierarchy.

clue.text: City has fresh lot of wine to entertain these league leaders

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a case is a box of a dozen bottles, a lot of wine

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A city side buys new wine to celebrate with the top teams of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'league leaders' look like a football reference; they are the first letters of 'these league', and 'to entertain' puts them inside the case of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in northeast England.

clue.text: Double time after instant messaging

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Repeat the timing after sending an instant message.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or copy, so the spitting image of someone is their double.

clue.text: Bundle in ditch

definitions.meaning: a bundle is British slang for a scuffle or fight
to ditch something is to discard it

explanation.surface: A heap of things lies in a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight, like a bundle, and to scrap is to throw away, to ditch.

clue.text: Missing a shot — ten players now

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are jumbled
missing means lacking, so the letter is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A team is now one shot short after ten players miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; take A out of TEN PLAYERS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently can mean at the present time, especially in Scottish and American usage.

clue.text: Brit with lasso — wild one in charge of cowboys

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British man with a rope goes wild while bossing the cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail boss leads the cowboys driving cattle along a trail.

clue.text: Books one left in a stateside hostel a long time ago

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the outer pieces

parts.note: the Y is American shorthand for the YMCA hostel
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
I is the Roman numeral one
quit is a past tense of leave, so left gives quit

explanation.surface: Volumes are abandoned by a resident of an American hostel long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y is the American name for the YMCA, a cheap hostel; 'in' puts the books, the one and the verb for left between A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquity means the distant past, the ancient period long ago.

clue.text: In succession to throne, oddly, viscount's last

indicators.note: oddly means in an odd way, so these letters are rearranged
last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An heir follows to the throne in a strange way after the viscount dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is not about odd letters; it rearranges TO THRONE, and T ends 'viscount's'.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot is British informal for consecutively, one after another.

clue.text: Plump single parent is best

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
I, the Roman numeral one, a single
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: An overweight single mother is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like 'fat' but is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable or best possible.

clue.text: Some Frenchman on air talking about a palace in Versailles

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the run is read backwards
some means part of, so the letters come from inside these words

explanation.surface: A Frenchman on the radio discusses a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NONAIRT spans 'Frenchman on air talking'; 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand and Petit Trianon are palaces in the grounds of Versailles.

clue.text: Sound colour: black

parts.note: plum is a dark purple colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A good colour for sound: black.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb the sea is to sound it, measuring the depth with a weighted line.

clue.text: American can have nothing against British actor

parts.note: a tin is a can
O, the figure zero, is nothing
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A US citizen can stand against a British performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Ustinov was a British actor and writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Ustinov was a celebrated British actor, writer and raconteur.

clue.text: Grow up with additive-free food?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the run is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: free of additives means no E, E being the European number code for food additives
grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: Children grow big on wholesome food without additives.
explanation.walkthrough: E-numbers are the European codes for food additives, so additive-free is NO E; NO E GRUB is read 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or flourish rapidly.

clue.text: Material a poet rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet

explanation.surface: Fabric is turned down by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a linen or cotton fabric, especially one printed with scenes.

clue.text: Appropriate directions followed by knight errant?

indicators.note: followed by puts the next piece after the first

parts.note: S and E are the abbreviations of the compass directions south and east
a knight errant rides out on a quest, so he is a quester

explanation.surface: A knight on a quest takes the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here (to take for oneself), not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester property is to seize or appropriate it legally.

clue.text: 13 right in the middle of Slough

indicators.note: in the middle of places one letter inside the other word

parts.note: to slough skin is to shed it

explanation.surface: A scrap of the right sort is found in the centre of an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town but is the verb, to shed. The definition is the answer to 13, SCRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a scrap, a small torn fragment.

clue.text: Wholehearted uplift for half-hearted music

indicators.note: uplift in a down clue means the word is raised, read backwards
half-hearted means half the doubled heart letters are taken away

parts.note: reggae is a style of Jamaican music

explanation.surface: Wholehearted enthusiasm gets a boost from listless tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: REGGAE has a double G at its heart; 'half-hearted' drops one to give REGAE, which 'uplift for' turns to EAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and wholehearted both describe keen, enthusiastic commitment.

clue.text: Regularly check computer screen

definitions.meaning: to keep watch on something over time
the display unit attached to a computer

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a computer screen regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to keep under observation, and a monitor is a computer's display.

clue.text: Unsophisticated young woman, sincere in appearing forward

indicators.note: appearing forward means the letters are moved to the front of the word

parts.note: genuine means sincere

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman is sincere when she appears forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a bold manner but moves IN from the end of GENUINE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is a naive young woman, especially as a stock stage role.

clue.text: Small Welsh county regarded as rich

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monmouthshire, a county in Wales
to eye is to regard or look at

explanation.surface: A small county in Wales is seen as wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Monmouthshire is a county in southeast Wales, shortened to MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having plenty of money, so rich.

clue.text: Capital unknown before taking lead

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
ere is an old word for before
the van is the leading part, the vanguard

explanation.surface: An unknown capital comes before a city taking the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerevan is the capital city of Armenia.
